question: The Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, had the goal of determining the sequence of how many billion base pairs that make up human DNA?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.0 billion base pairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Genome Project** (HGP) was an international scientific research project launched in **1990**, aimed at mapping and understanding all the genes in human DNA.
 
• The primary goal of the HGP was to determine the complete sequence of the **3 billion base pairs** that make up human DNA.
 
• DNA is composed of four chemical bases: **adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G)**, which are paired to form the rungs of the DNA double helix.
 
• The Human Genome Project was completed in **April 2003**, two years earlier than planned.
 
• The completion of the HGP marked a significant milestone in biological sciences, providing valuable insights into genetics, disease, and human evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goals of the Human Genome Project:**

 
 
• To identify all the approximately **20,000-25,000 genes** in human DNA.
 
• To determine the complete sequence of the **3 billion DNA base pairs**.
 
• To store this information in public databases for further research.
 
• To improve tools for data analysis and enable personalized medicine.
 
• To address ethical, legal, and social implications arising from genomic research.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Base Pairs in DNA:**
 
 
• The sequence of base pairs determines the **genetic instructions** for building proteins, which perform essential functions in the body.
 
• The pairing rules are specific: **A pairs with T**, and **C pairs with G**, ensuring accurate replication and functioning of genetic material.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of the Human Genome Project:**
 
 
• Discovery of genes associated with diseases like **cancer, Alzheimer’s, and cystic fibrosis**.
 
• Development of **genetic testing** for inherited conditions.
 
• Advancement in **personalized medicine**, allowing treatments tailored to individual genetic profiles.
 
• Increased understanding of **human evolution** and migration patterns through genetic studies.
 
 
 
• **Collaborating Organizations:**
 
 
• The HGP was a collaborative effort involving institutions from the **United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, France, Germany, and China**.
 
• It was coordinated by organizations like the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** and the **U.S. Department of Energy**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Genome Sequencing:**
 
 
• Used in **identifying genetic disorders** and developing targeted therapies.
 
• Plays a critical role in understanding genetic factors in diseases like diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular disorders.
 
• Enables advancements in **forensic science**, agriculture, and bioinformatics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline of the Human Genome Project:**

 
 
• Started in **1990** and completed in **April 2003**, ahead of schedule.
 
• Initial funding was provided by the **United States government**, followed by global collaborative investments.
 
 
 
• **Ethical Implications:**
 
 
• Raised concerns about **privacy, genetic discrimination, and ethical use of genetic information**.
 
• Prompted the development of legislation like the **Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA)** in the U.S.
